title: Tile-aware slab reservoir and decode-throttle for paged-attention cache resiliency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust allocator+eviction strategy to reduce KV fragmentation and tail decode latency under mixed workloads (many short chats + occasional long contexts). This ticket proposes a 'tile-aware slab reservoir' allocator combined with a decode-throttle controller that cooperates with kernel selection to reduce prefill stalls and reassembly overhead for paged attention.
background: Observed problems in production: when tenant traffic has a bimodal distribution (short bursts of many small requests + sporadic long-prefix requests), the paged KV cache becomes highly fragmented by small allocations. This leads to increased prefill latency (more page faults), kernel thrash (switching between small/micro kernels and large kernels), and occasional P99 tail spikes. Existing LRU-based reclamation does not prioritize reuse locality or compactability, and continuous prefill floods can cause contention on decode streams.
goal: Reduce P99 decode latency by 20-30% for mixed workloads and reduce fragmentation-induced page faults by 40% in representative bench harness. Keep steady-state throughput within 5% of current baseline.
proposed_design: 1) Tile-aware slab reservoir: partition KV memory into fixed-size 'tiles' (e.g. 64KB) and maintain a reservoir of free tiles grouped by class (hot, warm, cold) and by tenant affinity. Small allocations are served by assembling contiguous tiles from the reservoir with soft compaction rules to maintain compactable runs. Large allocations prefer contiguous runs to avoid scatter-gather during prefill.
proposed_design_continued: 2) Compactability score: each run has a compactability score computed from allocation age, continuity, and expected reuse rate (from telemetry). Eviction prefers low-compactability runs to avoid creating many tiny fragments.
kernel_and_scheduler_integration: 3) Kernel steering hints: allocator exposes tile histograms to kernel-selector. If hot small-tiles dominate, prefer microkernel with low startup cost; if contiguous runs exist, prefer high-throughput fused kernels. Kernel selection becomes a soft policy informed by allocator state.
prefill_and_throttling: 4) Decode-throttle controller: monitors prefill queue depth, KV page-fault rate, and per-tenant token backlog. When prefill pressure is high, controller introduces cooperative backpressure: slow down new prefill starts, prioritize continuation of in-flight decodes, and opportunistically compact adjacent free tiles during idle cycles.
reuse_and_reclamation: 5) Proactive reuse: for tenants with repetitive prefix patterns (chat sessions), we maintain lightweight token-range fingerprints to reuse prior runs without full prefill.6) Deferred reclamation: cold tiles are quarantined for a reclaim window to allow short-lived reuse and avoid churn.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Increased allocator complexity and memory overhead for tile metadata (expected ~0.5-1% heap).
- Potential latency on heavy compaction cycles; mitigated by running compaction opportunistically on idle epochs.
- Kernel steering is heuristic-driven; misprediction could cause suboptimal kernel choices. We'll add telemetry to detect oscillation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bench: P50/P95/P99 decode latency measured on mixed workload harness improved by target margins (P99 -20% vs baseline).
- Fragmentation: total number of free-slab fragments reduced by >=40% after steady-state run.
- CPU/GPU overhead: allocator metadata overhead <1.5% and no >5% drop in throughput.
- No regression on long-sequence throughput tests.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement tile allocator + compactability scoring and unit tests. Add metrics for tile histograms and fragment counts. Phase 2 (integration): wire allocator signals into kernel-selector and add decode-throttle controller. Phase 3 (canary): deploy to staging + 10% canary customers; iterate. Phase 4 (rollout): release with runtime-2.3 feature flag and dashboard charts.
measurements_and_dashboards: Add dashboard: tile utilization heatmap, fragment size distribution, prefill queue depth, per-tenant compactability score, kernel-choice distribution, and decode P99 heatmap. Link to benchmark harness: https://redwood.internal/bench/paged-attn-mixed-workloads (design doc).
links_and_artefacts: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Tile+Aware+Allocator+Design, PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4120, Bench results (initial): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/uid/bench-358921
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Triage and initial spec (Aisha). 2026-03-07: Spike implemented prototype allocator and simulated fragment reduction (~33%). 2026-03-10: Design review with infra and kernels teams; agreed on tile size sweep (32KB/64KB/128KB). Action: Liam to add kernel-hint API. 2026-03-12: Kernel-selector patch landed (feature flag off); prototype bench shows P99 improvement ~18% on default tile size.
open_questions:
- Best default tile size across GPU families? (HW teams to provide guidance)
- How to safely migrate existing tenants' in-memory layout during rolling upgrade? (need rollback strategy)
- Telemetry thresholds for decode-throttle trigger (TBD via stress testing).
next_steps: 1) Complete kernel-hint API and add unit tests (owner: Liam, est 3d). 2) Add dashboard panels and alerts (owner: Sloane, est 2d). 3) Run HW sweep on p4/p5/a100 (owner: Infra, est 4d). 4) Prepare canary rollout plan and runbook (owner: Ops).
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on compactability scoring formula and kernel-hint API safety (must be opt-in behind runtime-2.3 feature flag). Please verify that telemetry adds low overhead.
